This book has seven chapters. This page is chapter 1. It says what each chapter does, which file to open, and which Python packages that chapter needs.

Open the `.qmd` file to run the cells. Open the `.html` file to read the same lesson. Install every package once, from the project folder:

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

## Chapter 1 — Loading, integrating and exploring data

This page is the map of the book. It does not load data and it does not fit a model.

| | |
|---|---|
| Lesson | `index.qmd` |
| Reading page | `index.html` |
| Packages | None. The later chapters use the packages below. |

## Chapter 2 — From business information to analysis-ready data

A company keeps the same facts in several places: a spreadsheet, a CSV file, a JSON file, a database, a small web service, and a PDF. This chapter loads each one into a table.

| | |
|---|---|
| Lesson | `lessons/02b-data-loading.qmd` |
| Reading page | `lessons/02b-data-loading.html` |
| Practice notebook | `notebooks/02b-data-loading.ipynb` |
| Packages | `pandas`, `openpyxl`, `requests`, `pymupdf` |

## Chapter 3 — One analysis table from several sources

The files from chapter 2 are separate. This chapter joins them into one row per invoice, and writes a short dictionary of the columns.

| | |
|---|---|
| Lesson | `lessons/02c-exploratory-analysis.qmd` |
| Reading page | `lessons/02c-exploratory-analysis.html` |
| Practice notebook | `notebooks/02c-exploratory-analysis.ipynb` |
| Packages | `pandas`, `requests`, `openpyxl`, `matplotlib` |

## Chapter 4 — Exploratory analysis and data visualisation

The invoice table is ready. This chapter draws the graphs that show who the customers are, what they pay, and which invoices are late.

| | |
|---|---|
| Lesson | `lessons/02d-eda-visualisation.qmd` |
| Reading page | `lessons/02d-eda-visualisation.html` |
| Practice notebook | `notebooks/02d-eda-visualisation.ipynb` |

## Chapter 5 — From structured data to a predictive model

Which customers are likely to leave? This chapter fits a logistic regression on the customer table. It then fits the same kind of model with the customer messages added. Both models are scored on customers they did not see during the fit.

| | |
|---|---|
| Lesson | `lessons/02e-churn-text-ml.qmd` |
| Reading page | `lessons/02e-churn-text-ml.html` |
| Packages | `pandas`, `numpy`, `scikit-learn`, `matplotlib` |

## Chapter 6 — Economic optimization of customer targeting

A churn probability is not yet a decision. Contacting a customer costs money. Losing a customer costs money too. This chapter chooses whom to contact so that the expected cost is as small as possible, including when a budget limits the total spend.

| | |
|---|---|
| Lesson | `lessons/02f-campaign-targeting.qmd` |
| Reading page | `lessons/02f-campaign-targeting.html` |
| Packages | `pandas`, `numpy`, `matplotlib`, `scipy` |

## Chapter 7 — Comparing local models with cloud AutoML

The same customers can be sent to a cloud service that trains its own model. This chapter compares those probabilities with the logistic regressions from chapter 5, then repeats the campaign decision from chapter 6. Reading the page does not start a paid job.

| | |
|---|---|
| Lesson | `lessons/02g-cloud-automl.qmd` |
| Reading page | `lessons/02g-cloud-automl.html` |
| Packages | `pandas`, `numpy`, `scikit-learn`, `matplotlib`, `scipy` |
| Paid run only | `google-cloud-aiplatform`, `google-cloud-storage` |

## How to follow a chapter

Open the chapter and run the cells from top to bottom. Chapters 2, 3, and 4 use the HarborLink company. The data are synthetic. They do not need an external account. Chapters 5, 6, and 7 read the telco files already stored in `data/raw/telco/` and `data/processed/telco/`.

Every chapter with code uses the kernel named `data-extraction-lesson`. `jupyter` and `ipykernel` install that kernel. They are listed in `requirements.txt`.
